audit_findings.title: A cyclical inventory build is being perpetuated as the earnings level
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the filed 2025 real-estate-inventory cash outflow was $257.041 million, 162% of the $158.2 million anchor loss
audit_findings.mechanism: The inventory outflow depresses anchor OE and is then perpetuated through forecast growth and terminal value; with a negative anchor, higher positive growth also mechanically produces larger losses and lower values.
audit_findings.evidence: Net cash used in operating activities during the year ended December 31, 2025 was primarily driven by cash outflow of $257.0 million in real estate inventory, which was primarily related to our homes under construction and land acquisitions and development level of activity, an $18.8 million decrease in the net change in accrued expenses and other liabilities, a net decrease in accounts payable, partially offset by the $60.4 million increase in the net change in other assets and the $16.1 million increase in the net change related to pre-acquisition costs and deposits, inventory impairment, accounts receivable and compensation expense for equity awards.
audit_findings.explanation: The $257.0 million inventory outflow is demonstrated, but the record does not establish how much was recurring maintenance investment versus temporary accumulation, land growth spending, or timing. Its scale relative to the anchor makes it reasonably capable of changing the valuation materially. The reversed BEAR-to-BULL ordering is also a demonstrated consequence of applying positive growth to negative OE, not evidence that the economic cases are coherent.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $257.041 million inventory outflow by maintenance inventory, growth land and development spending, temporary timing changes, capitalized interest, and impairments; rerun OE and verify scenario ordering and formulas under a negative anchor.

audit_findings.title: The equity-DCF interest rail may not capture LGIH's predominantly capitalized financing cost
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed 2025 interest incurred was $126.847 million, cash interest paid was $120.533 million, and $45.543 million was charged through cost of sales
audit_findings.mechanism: An equity-level OE stream must include financing costs exactly once, whether recognized in cost of sales, retained in inventory changes, or otherwise reflected in operating cash flow; omission raises OE, while a second deduction would lower it improperly.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest and other financing costs are capitalized as cost of inventory during community development and home construction activities, in accordance with Accounting Standards Codification (“ASC”) Topic 835, Interest and expensed in cost of sales as homes in the community are closed.
audit_findings.explanation: The capitalization and cash-payment amounts are demonstrated, but an omission from OE is only an unresolved possibility because the supplied valuation lacks the calculation trace. The $120.533 million cash payment is large relative to the $158.2 million anchor loss, so failure to capture it exactly once could materially alter the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Provide a line-by-line 2025 OE reconciliation showing the $120.533 million cash interest payment split between interest released through cost of sales, interest remaining in inventory, financing-cost amortization, and cash-flow adjustments; then rerun only if the trace proves omission or duplication.

audit_findings.title: The joint-venture bridge may double count earnings already present in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $24.6 million, or approximately $1.01 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: If JV income or distributions remain in OE while the $24.6 million investment is added in the equity bridge, the same equity claim is represented in both operating PV and the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Income associated with our investment in unconsolidated entities was $ 1.9 million, $ 13.3 million and $ 12.8 million, within other income, net on the statement of operations for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the OE series purged all JV returns remains unresolved. Nevertheless, removing the entire $24.6 million bridge addition would reduce every scenario by only about $1.01 per share, versus reported values of negative $55.10 to negative $98.67 per share and a $55 market price. That cannot change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $24.6 million latest carrying value and document removal from OE of equity-method income and distributions, including filed 2025 income of $1.928 million and distributions of $4.801 million; correct the bridge or OE rail if duplication is confirmed.

audit_findings.title: The omitted FY2024 breaks the historical sequence used to characterize the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: computed $0 per share under the stated latest-non-positive anchor rule; filed FY2024 net income was $196.071 million
audit_findings.mechanism: FY2024 would enter the historical OE series and the anchor-selection consistency review, but the stated method still selects the latest actual because 2025 OE is non-positive.
audit_findings.evidence: Net income for the year ended December 31, 2025 was $72.6 million, a decrease of $123.5 million, or 63.0%, from $196.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission of an audited intervening year is demonstrated and weakens the historical narrative. It does not change the numerical anchor under the supplied rule: adding FY2024 cannot remove the fact that latest OE is negative $158.2 million, so the current scenario values remain unchanged unless the methodology itself is altered.
audit_findings.action: Compute FY2024 OE using the required depreciation fallback, restore it to the series, and rerun the anchor-selection and too-hard narrative checks to confirm the stated zero valuation effect.

audit_findings.title: Performance guarantees create contingent claims not visible in the debt-only bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; gross outstanding letters of credit, performance and surety bonds were $416.0 million at June 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Any probable underfunded completion obligation not already accrued or included in inventory cost-to-complete estimates would reduce future OE or require an equity-bridge liability adjustment.
audit_findings.evidence: In the event any such bonds or letters of credit are drawn upon, we would be obligated to reimburse the issuer of such bonds or letters of credit.
audit_findings.explanation: The guarantees are demonstrated, but their gross face amount is not a loss estimate and management states that draws are not probable. No filed amount establishes an unrecorded present claim. This is therefore a contingent, forward-looking exposure to monitor rather than a current valuation adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $416.0 million latest gross guarantees project by project to accrued liabilities, inventory development budgets, remaining cost-to-complete estimates, collateral, and expected releases; rerun OE or the bridge only for identified probable underfunded amounts.
